name: Sculpfun S9 10W
tagline: 10W Sculpfun's proven budget line: still popular for value-focused makers
tldr: Sculpfun S9 10W is the 10W SKU on the Sculpfun sculpfun s9 line. Before S30 Ultra, the S9 was Sculpfun's workhorse. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

priceRange.note: 10W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in ~6–10 min in our benchmarks
Photo fills at ~60–140 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo takes ~12–18 min
Works with LightBurn and LaserGRBL and accepts air assist, so used units are easy to set up
cons: Slightly wider ~0.10 mm spot: very fine photo detail is a little softer than on the lower-power S9
Beyond 5 mm, cutting needs several slow passes and an air pump
Discontinued: check diode hours, lens and belts before buying a used unit
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Sculpfun S9. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.

editorialDepth.advantages: Sculpfun S9 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 5 mm+ cutting in production. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: Which machine is the Sculpfun S9 10W?
faq.answer: It corresponds to the S9 Pro, which Sculpfun sold with a 10W optical diode, a claimed 0.06 mm focus and a 400 × 410 mm engraving area. The line has been succeeded by the S10 and S30 series. Most buyers now find it used or refurbished: Sculpfun listed a refurbished S9 Pro at $199 in October 2026.

faq.question: How fast does the S9 10W cut 3 mm and 5 mm wood?
faq.answer: In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 6–10 min at 3–8 mm/s. Around 5 mm basswood is the practical limit in one or two passes with air assist. Sculpfun's claim of 15 mm wood relies on many slow passes, and plywood cuts slower than basswood because of its glue layers.

faq.question: Is the extra money over the S9 5W worth it?
faq.answer: If you cut, yes. On our tracked listings the 10W costs roughly $100–150 more ($299–449 against $199–299), cuts a 3 mm square in about 6–10 min instead of 9–15 min, and fills photos three to four times faster. If you only engrave small signs and leather, the 5W remains enough.

standoutFeatures.title: Usable cutting on a budget frame
standoutFeatures.body: 3 mm basswood squares in about 6–10 min in our benchmarks, with 5 mm reachable in one or two passes.

standoutFeatures.title: Upgrade path through S30 Ultra heads
standoutFeatures.body: Sculpfun lists its S30 Ultra laser heads (11W, 22W, 33W) as compatible with the S9 frame, so a used S9 can take a stronger head later.

standoutFeatures.title: Low used price
standoutFeatures.body: Sculpfun listed a refurbished S9 Pro at $199 in October 2026; private sales often sit in the same range.
